name: Holy Grail Skin Co.
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports early-stage. Atlanta Magazine (Nov 2025) calls Holy Grail Skin Co. a "Newcomer" that launched in April, after about two years of R&D. It has one product (Elixir no. 1) sold DTC online, with US-only shipping and international expansion still to come. The founders are two Atlanta moms, and nothing indicates a parent company or acquisition. The Tracxn results are for different companies named "Holy Grail" or "HolyGrail" (incorporated 2019, YC-backed, a tech or carbon-capture ecosystem), not this skincare brand, so they don't show funding for it. No funding announcements for the skincare company appear anywhere in the evidence. Local awards and press are consistent with a small, recently launched brand.
founders_supported_explanation: Leah Matthews: fully supported. Her LinkedIn profile lists her as Co-Founder at Holy Grail Skin Co., Owner and Director at Studio Go (Jan 2015 to present), and Co-Founder and Director of Operations at Studio To Go (Oct 2017 to present). The website's 'Leah + Mary, Co-Founders' sign-off and the Atlanta Magazine article also back her role. Mary Peck: her name and co-founder role are supported. The site signs off as 'Leah + Mary, Co-Founders, Holy Grail Skin Co.', and Atlanta Magazine names Mary Peck and Leah Matthews as the pair who started the brand. However, no cited page gives Mary's last name alongside the 'Mary' in the site sign-off, so the link relies on inference from the article. Her background is empty, so no background claim fails. The failing item is the weak founder-title link: the sources never explicitly call Mary Peck 'Co-Founder' by full name. The article says Peck and Matthews launched the company and released Elixir no. 1, which supports founding but not the exact title. This makes the claim partially supported rather than fully supported.

name: Stellar Beauty Co.
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the agent's claim. Business Wire confirms Stellar Beauty Co. launched July 9, 2026, exclusively DTC at stellarbeautyco.com, with four products. Beauty Independent says the parents self-funded it and reports no VC. The brand has about 5,000 TikTok followers, a small footprint, and no retail distribution. Nothing suggests a parent company or acquirer. The Yahoo/Madison Reed and Tracxn results from the independent search concern other companies and do not apply. Minor discrepancies, such as Beauty Independent listing a $12 price low versus the press release's $16, do not affect the stage verdict.
founders_supported_explanation: Stella Dorazio is clearly shown as the founder of Stellar Beauty Co. The sources say she is a 12-year-old athlete and that a class project at age 9 led her to launch the brand (YPulse). However, several background details are not in any provided source. Nothing says she is a golfer; the sources only say "athlete". Nothing mentions her mother, Mallory, or any work with her mother on product research, formulation and packaging. The Beauty Independent page was cited but not provided, so it cannot confirm these details. The failed claims are the golfer detail and the mother/Mallory collaboration on research, formulation and packaging.

name: Burd Beauty
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the agent's claim. Burd Beauty launched on Oct 22, 2025 (PR Newswire) and was founded in 2025. It sells only DTC through burdbeauty.com, TikTok Shop and Instagram, with 2 SKUs (shampoo and conditioner, plus a bundle). Retail and salon expansion is only described as future ('will expand'). No funding round appears in the sources. The independent search results (Madison Reed, Burd Manufacturing) are about other companies. One caveat is that co-founder Julie Smolyansky is CEO of publicly traded Lifeway Foods. But the press release and about page present Burd as a venture of the sisters with their mom, not as a Lifeway subsidiary or product line, and the contact email is a personal Gmail address. Nothing shows ownership by a larger company, so it still counts as a very early-stage startup.
founders_supported_explanation: All three founders are shown as founders of Burd Beauty, and the details check out against the cited pages. Julie Smolyansky: the PR Newswire release quotes her as 'CEO of Lifeway Foods and co-founder of Burd Beauty' and describes her as a survivor and a mom ('As a survivor and as a mom'). The about page calls her 'CEO of Lifeway Foods and longtime activist for survivors of violence', and the Instagram bio lists her among the founders. Misha Burdeen: the PR Newswire release calls her 'co-founder of Burd Beauty' and gives her age as 15. The about page says she is 15 and that she and Leah 'decided to combine their obsession - beauty products, into a brand that funds action', and the release says the brand fights domestic and teen dating violence. Leah Burdeen: the release lists her as 17 and as co-founder (the 'Lead' is a typo), and the about page contains the same origin story. The Instagram bio lists both sisters as founders. The YouTube URL cited for Julie was not provided, but the other sources cover every claim.

name: VIBES Beverages
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports early stage. VIBES Beverages LLC officially launched May 15, 2026, so it is only months old. It has three SKUs, co-manufactured at Burma Brewing, and sells mainly DTC via Shopify plus kava bars. Retail is described only as "entering key markets" or "inquiries", with no named national chain. A five-person founding team is described, and the LinkedIn page shows 111 followers. No funding round appears anywhere in the evidence. The Tracxn results are for a different company named "Vibes" (investors like Accel, Fidelity, Series A/B), not this beverage brand. Nothing suggests ownership by a larger company. The "nationwide" and "Red Bull" language is aspirational marketing and not evidence of a large footprint.
founders_supported_explanation: All three founders are shown as co-founders of Vibes Beverages in the cited sources. Jason Croxford: the BevNET and Brewbound press releases and the Glow Getter release call him Co-Founder, and he is the media contact. Akash Gupta: the press release names him Co-Founder and Head of Marketing, and says he is an e-commerce growth strategist in digital acquisition, SEO, backlink development and affiliate marketing, and Co-Founder of Total Botanical Solutions, which works with kratom, kava, kanna, mushroom and hemp brands. Matthew Abate: his LinkedIn page lists Co-Founder at Vibes Beverages, Co-Founder at BrandOs Group, Chief Commercial Officer at Burma Brewing Company, and Co-Founder of Mitra9 Brands, described as a functional beverage company scaled into a multi-million-dollar brand. It also says he owned and operated a martial arts school. No claim failed.

name: Happy Panda
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports early stage. Happy Panda (drinkhappypanda.com) announced its official market launch via PR Newswire on Feb 2, 2026, so it launched very recently. The site is a DTC storefront that ships nationwide, and no national retail distribution appears. It lists only a few flavors, and the founders (Cameron James and Dr. Noor) present it as an independent startup with no parent company. No funding round is mentioned anywhere. The independent search results (Tracxn India entity, Panda Retail, Cheeky Panda, Asset Panda, Happy Panda Wayne) concern different companies with similar names and don't contradict this. The Tracxn 'no funding raised' line is tied to an unrelated Indian entity, so it is weak evidence, but nothing found points to a priced VC round. Recent launch, DTC-only footprint, no funding, and independence together fit the early-stage definition.
founders_supported_explanation: Every claim is backed by the cited pages. Cameron James is named as co-founder and CEO in the PR Newswire release and as Founder & CEO on the About Us page. The Yahoo Finance 'Doctor and Athlete' release, which calls him 'Cam' and the same release's co-founder, covers his background: deep roots in professional sports and fitness, accolades in music and high-level sales, meeting Dr. Noor in the health insurance sector, and driving direct-to-consumer strategy and lifestyle positioning. The same release says Dr. Noor holds a Master's in Public Health and triple specialty training in Internal Medicine, General Surgery, and OB/GYN. It also says she leads B2B relationships and ensures clinical credibility. Both are shown as founders of Happy Panda. The one wrinkle is a 'Cameron Jones' caption typo in the PR Newswire release, but its quote attributes the words to Cameron James, so it does not undermine the claim. No claim failed.

name: Sēkwl Beverage House
early_stage_explanation: Sēkwl launched on May 1, 2025, so it is well within the last 2 years. The evidence shows no priced VC round or outside funding. The Tracxn result is for a different company named "Beverage House" and doesn't apply. The brand is small: DTC plus Colorado local retail through a regional woman-owned distributor (SMNR Sales). LinkedIn mentions 50+ retail locations in Colorado and across the U.S., which is still a modest footprint and not national retail. It is an independent, founder-led company with its own small production facility in Arvada, and no parent company appears anywhere. The agent's "pre-seed" label is a guess, and funding is unknown, but the evidence supports the early-stage verdict.
founders_supported_explanation: All four people are shown as founders in the provided sources. The Arvada Economic Development page names Ryan Kelley, Shannon Eurich and John Walls as cofounders alongside Matthew Eaton. The PR Newswire release, Yahoo Finance and Prepared Foods pages say the four created the brand. Several background details are not in the provided pages, so some claims failed. Matthew Eaton: the role (Founder & Chief Beverage Officer), 'beverage lover and flavor innovator', and the health scare leading to turkey tail research are supported. The LinkedIn claim (prior responsible sourcing roles at Autodesk and VMware) is unsupported because no LinkedIn content was provided. Ryan Kelley: co-founder and Eaton's husband are supported. The 'financial wizard making it happen behind the scenes' quote is attributed to the Our Story page, which was not provided, so it is unsupported. Shannon Eurich: co-founder and 'one of Eaton's best friends' are supported. The 'sales powerhouse who could sell mushrooms to a forest' description is unsupported because the Our Story page was not provided. John Walls: co-founder, the Chief Storyteller and Head of Marketing & Communications title, and 'best friend' are supported. The 'storytelling alchemist' description is unsupported because the Our Story page was not provided.
